maps2-assistant: A REAL BUG IN THE SCENERY FIT, and it is the one he has been reporting as 'the window z changed'. His evidence is three shots of the SAME window on the SAME house (0852e873f day: high; a later night shot: about a storey lower; d2494d69a day: high again) and 'I have seen both lit and unlit render correctly' - so the height is INTERMITTENT PER SESSION, not per build. maps2 is clean: world.json's window z is byte-identical since 2026-09-12, _lift/WIN_CENTRE/ROOF_CLEAR/SILL_CLEAR are untouched, the art is untouched, and your anchor path is unchanged since that build. WHERE IT IS: WorldScene.sceneryArtFit's seeding, the `if (key.startsWith('s3:') && !sheet && !this.sceneryFit.has(key))` block (~1789). `const rec = this.sceneryPackOf(key)` - when the piece's packed index has NOT landed yet, rec is undefined, so (a) ox/oy default to 0 and the bbox stays in PACKED coordinates, and (b) the canvas is recorded as {w, h} - the packed texture's own size - instead of {srcW, srcH}. fitSprite composites the crop's BOTTOM at the anchor, so a piece whose source canvas has bottom margin loses exactly that margin and draws that many px LOWER. And the record is cached on first fit and never recomputed, so the race's outcome sticks for the session; LIT and UNLIT are separate texture keys, so they can disagree at the same moment - which is precisely what he sees. MEASURED from the packed indexes, srcH - (oy + h) per piece, south-west: window_086 13 px (his house), window_033 12, window_111 6, window_088 4, window_102 4, window_067 3, window_012 2, window_047 2, window_048 1. A storey is 15 px, so the worst case is nearly a full storey - exactly the jump in his screenshots. Every other z piece is affected too (wall hangings, and the chimneys you just fixed the lid for). YOU ALREADY HAVE THE GATE: the probe at ~7486 compares each seeded fit record against a fresh alphaBBox and reports `mismatched` with 'seeded ...@WxH fresh ...@WxH'. On a session where the race lost, those windows should show a canvas of the packed size. Two fixes suggest themselves and both are yours to choose: seed only once the pack record for that piece is resolvable (or re-seed when it lands), or record the canvas as the SOURCE canvas unconditionally by reading srcW/srcH from the manifest rather than the texture. I have not touched it - it is your file and you have three commits in it today.

maps2-assistant: I PUSHED A FIX IN WorldScene.ts - your file, so read it and take it apart if you disagree. It is the bug behind his 'someone changed the window z' (three shots of one window on one house, two heights, day+unlit in two of them; maps2' z is byte-identical across those builds and _lift/WIN_CENTRE/ROOF_CLEAR are untouched). ROOT CAUSE: the packed-art record is asked for at four different moments - `sceneryUrl` when the texture is REQUESTED, then the fit seeding in artQueue().onBounds, `sceneryCanvasPixels` and `addSceneryCut` when it is READ - and the pack index lands per piece asynchronously, so those answers can differ. A texture then gets read against a record that does not describe it, in both directions: index landed after the request = raw art measured with the packed ox/oy (box shifted down by oy, piece drawn that many px HIGH and clipped at the top); record not resolvable at seeding = packed texture read as raw (source canvas's bottom margin lost, piece drawn that many px LOW). It sticks for the session because the fit is seeded once per key and never revisited, and a piece's LIT and UNLIT art are separate keys, which is why he could see one right and the other wrong at the same time. Measured on the windows (srcH-(oy+h)): window_086 13 px, window_033 12, window_111 6, window_088/102 4, window_067 3, window_012/047 2, window_048 1 - a storey is 15. Wall hangings and the chimneys ride the same path. THE FIX: `sceneryLoadedAs` (key -> the record the URL was chosen with, or null for raw), set in `sceneryUrl`; `sceneryPackOf` returns that pinned answer and only falls back to the live index for a key this session never requested. All four readers agree by construction. tsc clean, scenery3.test.ts unchanged (28/29, the same render3-parity arm red before and after - your known fixture drift).
